what: Both Linker bubbles run about 22px past the panel's right edge and are clipped, so words are cut off mid-sentence ('packing the', 'point at', 'collect2: error: ld returned' loses its end).
evidence: Audit at 390: p.bubble.right right edge 22px beyond the panel (two bubbles). Cause: the bubble holds long no-wrap code (cpp-ch2.css:134 `.bubble code { white-space: nowrap }`) such as `collect2: error: ld returned 1`, so its min-content width exceeds the .talk column, and `.bubble.right { justify-self: end }` pushes the overflow to the right, where `.panel { overflow: hidden }` clips it. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-1-5/ev/ch2-p26-390.png
fix: Let long code in bubbles break. Before → After (why): `.caption code, .bubble code, … { white-space: nowrap }` (cpp-ch2.css:134) → `.caption code, .bubble code, … { white-space: nowrap }` plus `@media (max-width: 640px) { .bubble code { white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: break-word } }` (the nowrap rule protects short flags like `-std`, but a 30-character message must be allowed to wrap on a 300px bubble).

what: The chapter's `@keyframes blink` for the belt cursor replaces the engine's `blink` keyframes for character eyes, so on this page every character's eyes fade out completely and back in every 4 seconds instead of blinking briefly.
evidence: cpp-ch2.css:119 `@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }` vs comic.css:317 `@keyframes blink { 0%, 92%, 100% { transform: scaleY(1) } 95% { transform: scaleY(0.1) } }` used by `.motion .char .eyes { animation: blink 4s infinite }` (comic.css:321). Measured with getAnimations() at 390 on cpp/ch2.html: the eyes animation's keyframes are `{o:0, opacity:1} {o:0.5, opacity:0} {o:1, opacity:1}`; on ch1/ch3/ch4/ch5 they are the engine's scaleY frames. Same class of bug as the AUTHORING 'naming chapter widgets' house rule.
fix: Rename the chapter keyframe. Before → After (why): `.motion .belt-screen .cursor { animation: blink 1s steps(1) infinite } @keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: 0 } }` → `.motion .belt-screen .cursor { animation: belt-cursor 1s steps(1) infinite } @keyframes belt-cursor { 50% { opacity: 0 } }` (keyframe names are global; reusing an engine name silently changes every character on the page).

what: In the side-by-side compiler cards the messages wrap, so the caret and fix-it lines land on their own rows away from the column they mark: in p20 the `^` and `;` for semi.cpp:4:39 float under nothing, right after p19 taught 'the caret marks column 39'.
evidence: Measured at 390: semi.cpp g++ card 9 lines → 16 rendered rows, clang++ 7 → 13; header.cpp 6 → 10 / 6 → 9; wrongfix.cpp 15 → 30; conv.cpp 8 → 14, conv_w 8 → 17, conv_werror 7 → 18. Prompts also split the flag: `g++ -` / `std=c++23`. Cause: the engine rule comic-widgets.css:242 `.duo-card .term { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }` (already reported engine-wide by visual-rs-6-10, visual-rs-11-15 and visual-py-21-25; listed here as the C++ evidence). At 1280 p20 is fine. Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-1-5/ev/ch2-p20-390.png
fix: Fix in the engine as already proposed: render `.duo-card .term` through the `.term.wrap` per-line path (caret source lines never wrap) or let it scroll. Chapter-only stopgap: `<div class="duo compare">` → give those `<pre>`s `class="term wrap"`, so carets stay aligned.

what: Terminals in `.pair2` and `.duo-card` wrap anywhere, so flags break at their dash (`-std=c++23 -` / `Wall`, `[-` / `Wliteral-conversion]`) and clang's fix-it `static_cast<int>( )` splits into `static_cast<int>` / `( )`, even at desktop width.
evidence: cpp-ch4.css:18 and :22 `… { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }`. At 1280, p30 narrow.cpp g++ card 5 → 8 rows and clang++ 12 → 21; p31 silent.cpp 7 → 12; p32 narrow_var.cpp 8 → 13 and 10 → 17. The chapter's own sibling stylesheet says why this matters (cpp-ch1.css:123: 'a broken "-std" reads as two things'). Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-cpp-1-5/ev/ch4-p30-1280.png
fix: Stop forcing anywhere-wrapping on compiler output. Before → After (why): `.pair2 .term, .pair2 .code { font-size: 0.85rem; white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere }` → `.pair2 .term, .pair2 .code { font-size: 0.85rem }` and mark those terminals `class="term wrap"` (engine wrap breaks at spaces only and never wraps a caret's source line); same for `.duo-card .term, .duo-card .code` at :18 and the duplicate `.term.wrap` at :26 (already on the refresh list).

what: The case-file part keys are a hand-rolled toggle group (`.rp-keys button`, a near copy of the engine's `.anat-keys button`), so they miss the engine's press feedback, `touch-action: manipulation` and `user-select: none`, and the highlighted text animates a colour transition the design system removed.
evidence: cpp-ch2.css:63-67 copy `.anat-keys` (comic.css:191-193); measured at 390: `.rp-keys button` touch-action auto, user-select auto, no :active transform, while the page's `.anat-keys button` report manipulation/none/transform 160ms. cpp-ch2.css:61 `.rp-part { transition: background 200ms ease-out, box-shadow 200ms ease-out }` (DESIGN_SYSTEM §5 rule 1: colour changes are instant; the anatomy-line row of the motion audit removed exactly this).
fix: In cpp-ch2.js:132 render `<ul class="anat-keys rp-keys">` and delete the duplicated button rules at cpp-ch2.css:63-65 (keep only the ✓ mark rule). Before → After (why): `.rp-part { transition: background 200ms ease-out, box-shadow 200ms ease-out }` → `.rp-part { }` (no transition; a highlight is a state shown on press).

what: The conveyor belt's motion is over budget and fires on every Next press, keyboard included: each new box drops in for 420ms with the built-in ease-out, and the belt animates `background-position` for 600ms.
evidence: Stepped p10 at 390 with motion on: animations `belt-drop` 420ms on li.bx.new and `belt-roll` 600ms on .belt-band.go per step (getAnimations). cpp-ch2.css:111-115. Under reduced motion both are removed, but nothing fades in its place (DESIGN_SYSTEM §5 rule 5 keeps a short fade for entrances that show what changed).
fix: Before → After (why): `.motion .bx.new { animation: belt-drop 420ms ease-out 1 }` from `translateY(-26px)` → `animation: belt-drop var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) both` from `translateY(-12px) scale(0.95)` + opacity (an entrance on a 10+/minute stepper stays under 300ms, strong curve); `belt-roll 600ms linear` on background-position → `transform: translateX()` on a pseudo-element stripe for ≤280ms, or delete it (non-GPU property; the box drop already shows the movement); add `.bx.new` to the engine's reduced-motion fade list via `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .motion .bx.new { animation: fade-in var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out) both !important } }`.

what: The NEW file tile in the session walker pops in for 380ms with the built-in ease-out on every Next press, slower than the engine's own `pop-in` timing.
evidence: cpp-ch1.css:57 `.motion .ses-file.new { animation: pop-in 380ms ease-out 1 }`; measured per step at 390: pop-in 380ms on li.ses-file.new next to the engine's 200ms tracer pop-in. No fade under reduced motion.
fix: Before → After (why): `animation: pop-in 380ms ease-out 1` → `animation: pop-in var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) both` (same keyframes as the engine's .tr-new; under 300ms, strong curve, fills before the first frame).

what: Odometer digits roll with a keyframe that restarts on every click and uses the built-in ease-out with no opacity, so rapid +1 clicks jitter.
evidence: cpp-ch3.css:97-98 `.motion .odo-digit.roll { animation: odo-roll 260ms ease-out 1 }` from `translateY(-40%)`; cpp-ch3.js:87 removes and re-adds the class on each click (keyframes restart from zero; STANDARDS 'Interruptibility').
fix: Before → After (why): `odo-roll 260ms ease-out` from `translateY(-40%)` → `odo-roll var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)` from `translateY(-25%); opacity: 0.4` (short, strong curve; a smaller travel hides restarts on rapid clicks).
